S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
examples: Continually procrastinates or is reluctant to start writing long reports or complex homework.
Avoids activities that require long periods of concentration, such as reading books or studying.
Passes off tasks that require complex thinking or planning to others.
Gets annoyed or resists when asked to start a task that requires significant mental effort.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation, is a neurodevelopmental condition marked by persistent inattention-related difficulties that impair functioning across settings, with hyperactive-impulsive signs present but not dominant. It is typically chronic, often recognized when life demands exceed established coping routines, and is distinguished from mood, anxiety, sleep, or cognitive disorders by a longstanding pattern of executive-function difficulty not limited to a single episode or stressor.

patient.stressor: Deborah enrolled in an evening administrative-management certificate program to strengthen her path toward an Office Manager role while continuing her full-time secretary position. During the next 15 months, the combined school-and-work load strained the routines that had previously kept her functioning: she had trouble organizing class materials and office tasks, delayed readings or assignments that required sustained effort, misplaced planners and flash drives, and became distracted by classroom noise, office interruptions, or unrelated thoughts. She remained generally reliable but began forgetting minor appointments, registration steps, and household errands, and classmates noticed her fidgeting and stepping out during longer sessions. After a course advisor suggested she seek support for attention and study-management difficulties, Deborah asked her primary care clinician for a referral to psychiatry.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: I can usually keep up at work, but since starting the evening classes my desk, class folder, and email reminders all turn into piles, and I waste time figuring out what I’m supposed to do first.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
S006.manifestation: If an assignment means sitting down to read a long chapter or write out a plan, I keep putting it off until it’s late and then I’m rushing through it after work.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: I’m always setting down my planner, flash drive, or keys somewhere and then spending ten minutes checking my purse, car, and office drawers before I can move on.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: At the office or in class, one phone ringing, people talking nearby, or even a random thought about something at home can pull me off what I was working on.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: What finally made me ask for help is that I keep forgetting little things I normally handle, like returning calls, turning in a registration form, or stopping for an errand on the way home.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: During longer classes I notice myself clicking my pen, bouncing my foot, or shifting around in the chair even when I’m trying to sit still and pay attention.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: In the three-hour evening sessions, I’ll find reasons to get up for water or step into the hallway for a minute, not to be disruptive but because staying seated the whole time feels hard.

add_requirements.Onset prior to age 12 years: Even in elementary school, I was the kid who forgot permission slips, lost homework in my backpack, and needed my mother or teacher to remind me step by step to finish projects.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m still getting by, but I’ve missed small work follow-ups and school deadlines often enough that I worry it could affect my reputation and my chance at moving into an Office Manager role.
add_requirements.duration: These attention and organization problems have been noticeably harder to manage since I started the evening certificate program about 15 months ago.
